doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

title: Missing the Creole Fiesta in 1960-61; riding in the 1962 parade
summary: The Fiesta was skipped in 1960 and 1961 because of illness; Edna describes dressing and riding in this year's parade.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Which year didn't they have the Creole Fiesta? One year you missed? Because you were sitting in the hospital that same year.
Yeah. 1961. 60. Oh, 61. We missed 61. Last year in 61, you missed 61.
Oh, yes. We were in the hospital a whole year of 61. Oh, a whole year, yes. But we had the parade in 59, now you have 62. Oh, yes, we had 59.

We missed 60 and 61, you see. We stopped in September. September. And so we had half a year each week. You see, half a year each week. So we, they wanted to go on, but they had started now, too. Before it would be a failure, rather being a failure, I'd rather not have it at all. And you see how we came out this year? Everybody was all talking how nice it was. You saw it? We saw it. Wasn't it nice?
It was very nice. I wasn't going to ride.

I was sitting here, he didn't know. What are you going to do? I said, well, listen, I'll let you know the day of the parade. So about Friday, I had taken my dress down and shook it up and had it. I said, well, if I feel good, I'm going to ride. If I don't feel good, I'll sit on the porch. I'll dress up and sit right on the porch and watch the parade go by. So that's the way we had it. And the members, oh, let's pray for Ms. Senegal to ride. Let's pray for her to ride, because her heart and soul is in it. I said, no, not my soul. My heart is in it, but not my soul. I'm bringing my soul to God. And so they were all in the patio and I didn't... Have you seen my patio? No. Oh, I want you to... You have?

Oh, I want you to see my patio. How pretty do you. They all were in my patio and one or two of them would fall into the back. I was dressing in here and taking my time. I didn't want to go out there because I didn't want to see you. I said, maybe they'd make me nervous, and I was here. So that's it. I said, oh, how have they put my earrings on? I was getting nervous. I said, oh, but you're right. I said, don't you see I'm dressed? Sure, right. Just help me put your earrings on. And so, and he was there. He knew I was getting ready. And so when I came out, I said, there she is. There she is. She's going to ride. She's going to ride. And all of them were so glad to see me. I said, well, you ought to just say a little prayer for me. I'll ride. And I didn't feel numb the worst part. I took some of my heart medicine, though. I took some of that.
She couldn't get excited on the music because she's accustomed to it.
And there was no excitement that I was on. There was something strange for, you know what I mean.

If there was any strange, any strange excitement that I wasn't, but I was used to all that kind of excitement, so it didn't worry me. It didn't worry me, at least. And there was a little, they didn't want me to know of anything. There was a little misunderstanding going on in the carriage back of me. They wouldn't tell me about it until after it was all over with. I said, we had told you it made you nervous, so we just ironed it out ourselves. I said, well, that's the thing to do. I said, if you all do that, I'll live a long time. I said, we want you to enjoy it.
